ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $CD=3\text{cm}$, and point P is a moving point on $AB$. Connect $DP$. What is the minimum value of $DP$ in cm?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $DP'\perp AB$ at $P'$,\\
since $AD$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, and $DP'\perp AB$,\\
therefore $DP'=DC=3$ cm,\\
hence, the minimum value of $DP$ is $\boxed{3}$ cm.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a right triangle ABC with C the right-angle vertex, AC vertical, CB horizontal, D on CB, AD drawn from A to D, and P constrained to lie on side AB. From the text, use that AD is the angle bisector at A, CD=3 cm, and P moves along AB. Since D lies on the angle bisector AD, D has equal perpendicular distances to the two sides of angle A, namely AC and AB. In the diagram CD is perpendicular to AC because CD lies on CB and AC ⟂ CB, so the distance from D to AC is CD=3. Therefore the perpendicular distance from D to AB is also 3. Among all segments DP with P on AB, the shortest is the perpendicular from D to AB, so the minimum DP is 3 cm.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as placing C at the left-bottom right angle, A above C, B to the right, D on the horizontal side CB, and P variable on the slanted side AB. Use coordinates: set C=(0,0), A=(0,a), B=(b,0), so D=(3,0) because CD=3. From the text, AD is the angle bisector, so by the angle bisector theorem in triangle ABC, CD/DB=AC/AB, i.e. 3/(b-3)=a/sqrt(a^2+b^2). The line AB has equation ax+by-ab=0. The perpendicular distance from D=(3,0) to line AB is |3a-ab|/sqrt(a^2+b^2)=a(b-3)/sqrt(a^2+b^2). Using the angle-bisector-theorem relation gives a(b-3)/sqrt(a^2+b^2)=3. Since the minimum of DP for P on AB occurs at the perpendicular projection of D onto AB, the minimum DP is 3 cm.
